Pattern: itemise + N; thường bị động
Examples: The bill was itemised only after a complaint. | They itemise every expense for the accounts.

Pattern: stash + N + in/away + N
Examples: She stashed the cash in a tea tin for forty years. | He stashed nine hundred away without telling anyone.

Pattern: a well-paid + N (job, post)
Examples: A well-paid job in that town means thirty thousand. | The best-trained staff are not the best paid.

Pattern: a low-paid + N (worker, sector)
Examples: Low-paid work carries the highest rate of in-work poverty. | Nine low-paid sectors employ most of the ward.

Definition: kiếm bằng mồ hôi nước mắt
Pattern: hard-earned + N (money, savings)
Examples: Hard-earned savings went on a roof that should have lasted. | Nobody risks hard-earned money twice.

Pattern: be + out-of-pocket; out-of-pocket + expenses
Examples: Volunteers are left out-of-pocket for their own fares. | Out-of-pocket expenses are claimed quarterly.

Pattern: a non-refundable + N (deposit, fee)
Examples: The non-refundable deposit was four hundred. | Nine non-refundable fees preceded one refusal.

Pattern: an itemised + N (bill, statement)
Examples: An itemised bill exposed the duplicate charge. | They send an itemised statement every quarter.

Pattern: second-hand + N (furniture, car)
Examples: Second-hand furniture outlasts most of the new. | They bought everything second-hand and kept it for decades.

Pattern: a good-value + N (meal, product)
Examples: The canteen is good-value and nobody mentions it. | A good-value tool is the one that is still there in nine years.

Pattern: be + free-of-charge
Examples: The advice is free-of-charge and independent. | Nine services that were free-of-charge now carry a fee.

Pattern: a paid-up + N (member, subscription)
Examples: She has been a paid-up member since 1991. | Only paid-up members may vote at the meeting.

Pattern: put by + N hoặc put + N + by; tách được
Examples: They put by a little each week for the winter fuel. | She had nine hundred put by and no intention of spending it.

Pattern: run short of + N; không tách được
Examples: They ran short of money in the third week every month. | The kitchen ran short of everything by Thursday.

Pattern: come into + N (money, an inheritance)
Examples: She came into a small inheritance at fifty. | He came into money and changed very little.

Pattern: live off + N; không tách được
Examples: They lived off savings for nine months. | She lives off a pension and a lodger.

Pattern: do without + N; không tách được
Examples: They did without a car for twenty years. | She can do without most things except the telephone.

Pattern: stump up + N hoặc stump up for + N
Examples: Somebody had to stump up for the repair. | They stumped up nine hundred between four households.

Pattern: chip away at + N; không tách được
Examples: They chipped away at the debt for four years. | She chips away at the balance every pay day.

Pattern: settle up; settle up with + sb
Examples: They settle up at the end of each month. | He settled up with his brother after nine years.

Pattern: pay up; không có tân ngữ
Examples: The company paid up only after the tribunal. | They paid up in full and said nothing.

Pattern: scrape together + N; tách được
Examples: They scraped together the deposit from four relatives. | She scraped nine hundred together in a fortnight.

Pattern: every penny counts
Examples: On that income every penny counts. | Every penny counts when the margin is a bus fare.

Pattern: watch the pennies
Examples: They watched the pennies and the pounds looked after themselves. | She has watched the pennies since 1979.

Pattern: run/live + on a shoestring
Examples: The club runs on a shoestring and nine volunteers. | They lived on a shoestring for the first two years.

Definition: sửa dùng tạm thay vì mua mới
Pattern: make do and mend
Examples: Make do and mend was not nostalgia; it was arithmetic. | They made do and mended for a decade.

Pattern: be + worth every penny
Examples: The proper boots were worth every penny. | Nine hundred for that repair was worth every penny.

Pattern: count sth + down to the last penny
Examples: She accounted for it down to the last penny. | The fund was spent down to the last penny.

Pattern: cost + a pretty penny
Examples: The repair cost a pretty penny and saved the roof. | That car cost a pretty penny in its day.

Pattern: balance the books
Examples: She balanced the books every Sunday for forty years. | Balancing the books meant one fewer meal out.

Pattern: be + strapped for cash
Examples: They were strapped for cash until the invoice cleared. | Everybody is strapped for cash in the last week of January.

Pattern: rob Peter to pay Paul
Examples: Consolidating like that robs Peter to pay Paul. | They robbed Peter to pay Paul for nine months.
